text.verify_both_storefront_actions_work_agai: Verify live availability and delivery for all products after in-flight work and any 5-second cooldown finish.
text.in_network_faults_click_clear_all_faults: In Network Faults, clear all faults and restore default settings: both fallbacks off, both timeouts 3000 ms. Resetting answers does not reset runtime settings.
text.how_to_restore_default_behavior_after_an: How to restore default behavior after an experiment
text.blast_radius_means_which_customer_action: Blast radius is the impact beyond the lamp. An abort condition tells you when to stop and clear faults. Fast Shipping failure can break the catalog without filling workers.
text.the_period_you_measure_in_each_phase_use: Use fresh, equal windows of 60–90 seconds. Grafana rates span one minute; let the previous phase leave the window.
text.the_charts_you_read_during_the_experimen: Charts for latency, errors and fallbacks. p95 estimates the time 95% of requests fall at or below; 1.5 s equals 1500 ms.
text.the_measurement_collector_it_asks_the_se: Collects service metrics every five seconds and supplies Grafana. Raw queries are optional.
text.the_useful_response_storefront_returns_w: An honest partial result: unconfirmed stock or an unavailable quote. Enabling fallback also enables a breaker that pauses failed product/dependency calls for 5 seconds before one probe.
text.how_long_storefront_will_wait_for_a_depe: The dependency wait limit after a request is admitted. A short timeout releases workers sooner; the queue has a separate 1000 ms limit.
text.the_problem_you_introduce_in_network_fau: A delay or disconnect added in Network Faults. It changes the real local request path.
text.your_measurements_with_normal_service_be: Measurements taken before a fault. Compare later runs against them.
text.what_do_baseline_timeout_fallback_and_th: Terms and cleanup · expand to review
text.optional_api_and_terminal_examples_the_w: Optional API and terminal examples. The workshop can be completed with the browser controls.
text.collects_service_metrics_every_five_seco: Collects service metrics every five seconds and supplies Grafana. Optional for raw queries; no input needed for the guided challenges.
text.read_charts_of_response_times_failures_a: Read charts of response times, failures, and fallback use.
text.inject_a_fault_then_use_the_fallbacks_ti: Inject a fault, then use the Fallbacks & timeouts tab to enable a mitigation. All controls work on Windows and Mac.
text.network_faults_create_the_problem_and_te: Network Faults · create the problem and test a response
text.click_check_availability_and_order_previ: Click Check availability and Order preview; read the result and request time.
text.windows_start_bat_stop_bat_mac_start_com: Windows: start.bat / stop.bat · Mac: start.command / stop.command. In a source checkout, these files are at the repository root.
text.use_storefront_network_faults_and_grafan: Use Storefront, Network Faults and Grafana. Submit your notes to unlock the next challenge.
text.open_challenge_1_in_the_sidebar_its_brie: Open Challenge 1 for its tasks. Expand the general five-step guide here whenever you need it.
text.extract_the_zip_start_docker_desktop_the: Extract the ZIP, start Docker Desktop, then double-click start.bat (Windows) or start.command (Mac).
text.the_shop_normally_starts_healthy_in_chal: Start healthy. Add faults yourself in Challenges 1, 2 and 4; ask a partner to seed a hidden fault in Challenge 3. Opening or submitting a challenge does not change the shop.
text.you_are_the_engineer_responsible_for_a_l: Desk Lamp, Task Chair and Writing Desk share Inventory, Shipping and two Storefront workers. Only the lamp’s network paths can be faulted.
text.make_a_working_shop_fail_then_improve_it: Contain one product’s fault before it disrupts the catalog
text.investigate_a_small_storefront_through_f: Follow the Chaos Engineering process. Compare the same incident before and after containment. Could you find and mitigate the fault?
text.all_answers_reset_challenge_1_is_availab: All answers reset. Challenge 1 is available.
text.reset_all_answers_this_clears_every_draf: Reset all answers? This clears every draft and submitted answer in this browser and locks Challenges 2–4 again. Download your notes first if needed. This does not reset Docker, network faults, or mitigations.

challengeTitles.challenge-1: One slow product blocks the shop
challengeTitles.challenge-2: One missing quote breaks the catalog

challengeSummaries.title: 1 · A slow lamp blocks healthy products
challengeSummaries.description: Watch shared workers fill, then protect other products with a fallback.

challengeSummaries.title: 2 · A missing quote hides the catalog
challengeSummaries.description: Disconnect lamp Shipping, then shrink the impact from the complete delivery catalog to one unavailable quote.

challengeSummaries.title: 3 · Find how the incident spreads
challengeSummaries.description: Diagnose a hidden lamp fault from catalog failures, healthy-product impact and real worker indicators.

challengeSummaries.title: 4 · Prove useful containment
challengeSummaries.description: Design an experiment whose mitigation visibly protects the catalog or healthy products, and document its trade-off.

guide.title: How to run an experiment · five steps
guide.description: Use this process for each challenge. The challenge page contains its own detailed tasks.

steps.title: Steady State
steps.instruction: Measure the healthy baseline. Start with default settings. Measure how the system behaves under healthy conditions. Check Storefront and Grafana.

steps.title: Hypothesis & Fault Injection
steps.instruction: State the expected impact a fault would have. Then apply the fault.

steps.title: Measure impact.
steps.instruction: Compare customer results, dependencies, shared workers, queue and rejections over 60 to 90 second.

steps.title: Choose a mitigation
steps.instruction: Use evidence to choose a mitigation. For example a timeout and fallback. Explain what you expect your mitigation to improve.

steps.title: Repeat, compare and clean up
steps.instruction: Retest the identical fault and traffic. Record improvements. Clear faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.
